summary: 2 of 11 proposals recover the withheld algorithm-to-lower-bound conversion: P10 and P11 each describe supplying a modest ACC0 circuit-satisfiability algorithm and converting its existence, via nondeterministic time-hierarchy / indirect-diagonalization machinery with succinct completeness translations, into an unconditional NEXP-not-in-ACC0-style bound, with the algorithm-first coupling stated as load-bearing; both explicitly clear the distinctness guard against the conditional PIT bridge and the refutation skeleton. P02 is the strongest partial: it adopts the supplied-algorithm, algorithm-first posture but on the identity-testing bridge without hierarchy machinery (TRAIN-near per the guard). P08 partially overlaps on hierarchy/indirect-diagonalization machinery but preserves the refutation (assumption-to-contradiction) skeleton and supplies no algorithm (TRAIN-near). The remaining seven (P01, P03, P04, P05, P06, P07, P09) pursue property-based, amplification-based, proof-complexity, or GCT directions with none of the three criteria present. No proposal required a cannot_assess verdict; all verdicts are ModelJudgment on described content only, with no generous completion supplied on any proposal's behalf.
